title: Cordless Power Scrubbers for Stiff Hands: Two Options With Posted Prices, and What They Can't Do
subtitle: A battery-powered brush can ease some of the back-and-forth of scrubbing, but it will not remove heavy stains on its own or reduce how much you need to grip.
excerpt: If scrubbing the tub or tile leaves your hands and wrists aching, a cordless power scrubber can handle the scrubbing motion. Here is how they work, what to check before buying, and two options with posted prices, plus what they cannot do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Scrubbing a bathtub or a stretch of tile is hard on the body. You grip a brush tightly, push down, and move your wrist back and forth for minutes at a time. For anyone with stiff fingers, sore wrists or a cranky back, that chore can go from tiresome to painful.

A cordless power scrubber is a battery-powered brush that makes the scrubbing motion for you. You hold it against the dirty surface and let the motor work. It will not clean on its own, you still have to hold it, and it does not make bathroom cleaning risk-free.

There are two main styles. A spin scrubber has a round brush head that spins. An oscillating scrubber has a head that moves back and forth instead of spinning. Either way, the motor supplies the motion.
Some models come with a long pole so you can reach high or low spots without bending. Smaller handheld models have no pole, so they suit counters and tile within easy reach.
Consumer Reports, which tested eight models, points to one feature above the rest. As its testing lead Dan Kahl put it:
"The biggest difference between a good electric power scrubber and a subpar one is actually battery life." Dan Kahl, Consumer Reports

According to Consumer Reports, the models with the shortest battery life ran only about 10 minutes, which may not get you through a full tub. Consumer Reports also says comfort and design matter for how easy a scrubber is to use.

items: Runtime: Look for a stated battery runtime, and remember that bigger jobs like a whole shower need more of it.

Battery type: A rechargeable model may only work with that maker's batteries, and the manual may have charging rules, such as when to recharge. AA-powered models are simple, but you will keep buying batteries.
Weight: A tool with a pole can still tire a weak grip or wrist. If possible, compare listed weights before you buy.
Reach: An extension pole can help you avoid bending and stretching. Without one, the tool is best for counters and tile within easy reach.
Speed settings: Some models have low and high speeds. Check what the product page lists.
Water resistance: Check how the maker describes it. One model here is called waterproof, but not for long submersion, and the other is only "water resistant." Do not submerge either one.
Brush heads: Several head shapes may help with different surfaces. Check whether replacement heads are sold.
Warranty and returns: Check the maker's warranty (the Sun Joe below lists 2 years) and the store's return policy in case the weight or grip does not suit you.

sections.content: Spinning heads can spray suds and splatter, so wear clothes you do not mind getting wet. Neither tool removes heavy grout stains or mildew by itself, so you will still need a cleaning product. The scrubber supplies the motion, not the cleaning power.
Check the manual for charging and care instructions before you start, especially for the battery.

A power scrubber does nothing to help your balance. Never stand unsteadily on the edge of a tub or lean far over a slippery floor to reach a spot. Use the pole from steady footing, hold a grab bar if you have one, and leave the hardest-to-reach spots for a helper. If you have hand or wrist pain or stiffness, talk with your doctor before relying on any tool to get through cleaning, and see them sooner if the pain is getting worse.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A power scrubber will not make cleaning day disappear, but it may make some of the work easier on your hands. Pick the size that fits your home and your grip, and take it slowly.

products.name: Sun Joe 24-Volt Cordless Handheld 360-Degree Spin Scrubber Brush Kit with 1.3 Ah Battery + Charger (24V-PWSCRB-LTW)
products.price: $72.32 (Home Depot, seen November 2026; check current price)
products.blurb: Suits people who want to reach high or low without bending, with a pole that extends from 27 to 50 inches. It has two speeds, four brush heads, up to 50 minutes of runtime and a 2-year warranty, but it takes only Sun Joe batteries. At 3.5 pounds it may still tire a weak grip or wrist.

products.name: Rubbermaid Power Scrubber with 2 Scrubbing Heads (Reveal), Model 2057486
products.blurb: A low-cost handheld choice for counters and tile within easy reach. It has an oscillating head, a grout head and four included AA batteries, but no extension pole. The maker claims it cleans "up to 2X faster than manual scrubbing," it is described only as "water resistant," and its page showed no reviews.
